chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Writing "Pastels" and the Erroll Garner and Ross Russell session
summary: He wrote "Please Let Me Forget", Garner played it back by ear, and Ross Russell renamed it "Pastels" at a recording date; "Trio" was made up by Callender, Garner and Doc West.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: The same with Erroll Garner. Now, Erroll's first hit tune, "Pastels," you might have heard it...

That was my tune. So he and I and Doc West were... I was living actually on 25th Street, but they lived on 28th Street (that's on the east side), and I used to be there so much until I considered myself living there, too. We used to just hang out together. And there was an old raggedy piano, and I sat down one day and played "Pastels," which when I wrote it was called "Please Let Me Forget." It was actually my torch for some girl I had been in love with who didn't know I was alive.
So now it comes out! [LAUGHS] Erroll had ears like you wouldn't believe. So after I had played it, he sat down and started playing it.

So Ross Russell got us together to record with Charlie Parker and Wardell Gray and Dexter Gordon and Howard McGhee and...let's see, maybe some other people, but those are the ones that come to mind. So after we had finished with Charlie Parker one day, Ross said, "Do a couple of things." So we did "Pastels," and after that we played another thing which we had made up called "Trio." Well, the three of us had actually made that up, although Erroll Garner's name is

on it alone; but he and I and Doc West made it up together. And a lot of people had thought that Erroll wrote "Pastels," and a lot of disk jockeys thought so -- but it finally got straightened out who actually wrote it.
And incidentally, Ernie Andrews just made a record on it, put it on an album. I have to get you a copy of it.
Yeah, I'd love to hear that. So how did the title get changed?
Ross Russell...you may know him or have heard of him...
He said, "'Please Let Me Forget' seems too long. Let's change it to 'Pastels.'" So I said, "okay." So later I changed some of the lyrics to make it coincide with "Pastels."
